Consider a spherical shell of radius $\mathrm{r}$ and radial thickness dr. $P \& P+d P$ are pressure at its inner and outer surface. Let $\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{r}}=$ gravitational acceleration at distance $\mathrm{r}( \lt \mathrm{R})\sum_{\downarrow} \mathrm{P}_{0}=$ Atmospheric pressure
For equilibrium of this shell - $\begin{array}{l} ($P+d P)$\left($4 $\pi$r^{2}\right)+$\left($4 $\pi$r^{2} d r\right) \rho g_{r}=(P)$\left($4 $\pi$r^{2}\right) \\ $\left$\{\rho=$\frac{3 M}{4 \pi R^{3}}=\right.\text{ Density of sphere }$\\ \Rightarrow \quad d P=-\rho g_{r} d r \\ \because \quad g_{r}=$\frac{4}{3} \pi \text{ Gpr }$\\ \Rightarrow \quad $\mathrm{dP}=-\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{G} \rho^{2}$r d r \end{array} $\{(-)$ ve sign indicates that pressure is decreasing with radius $\}$ $\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \int_$P^{P_{0}} d P=\int_r^{R}-$\frac{4}{3} \pi$G \rho^{2} r d r \\ \Rightarrow & P_{0}-P=-$\frac{4}{3} \pi$G \rho^{2}$\left(\frac{R^{2}}{2}-\frac{r^{2}}{2}\right)$\\ \Rightarrow & P=P_{0}+$\frac{4}{3} \pi$G \rho^{2}$\left(\frac{R^{2}}{2}-\frac{r^{2}}{2}\right)$\\ & P=P_{0}+$\frac{3 G M^{2}}{8 \pi R^{4}}\left($1-$\frac{r^{2}}{R^{2}}\right) \end{array}$Hence $P \propto \frac{1}{\mathrmR^{4}}\Rightarrow$ Average pressure will also be proportional to $\frac{1}{\mathrmR^{4}}\Rightarrow$ correct answer is $[\mathrm{A}]$

The periods of revolution of $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ are $3 \mathrm{ h}$ and $24 \mathrm{ h}$ respectively. The radius of the orbit of $S_{1}$ is $3 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{ km}$. Then the orbital speed of $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ as observed from
options: the planet is $4 \pi \times 10^{4} \mathrm{ km} \mathrm{ h}^{-1}$ when $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ is closest from $\mathrm{S}_{1}$.
the planet is $2 \pi \times 10^{4} \mathrm{ km} \mathrm{ h}^{-1}$ when $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ is closest from $\mathrm{S}_{1}$.
$S_{1}$ is $\pi \times 10^{4} \mathrm{ km} \mathrm{ h}^{-1}$ when $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ is closest from $\mathrm{S}_{1}$
$S_{1}$ is $3 \pi \times 10^{4} \mathrm{ km} \mathrm{ h}^{-1}$ when $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ is closest from $\mathrm{S}_{1}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrmT^{2} \propto \mathrmr^{3}$
$\begin{array}{l} \frac{9}{24^{2}}=\left(\frac{3 \times 10^{4}}{r^{3}}\right)^{3} \\ \frac{3 \times 3}{24 \times 24}=\left(\frac{3 \times 10^{4}}{r}\right)^{3} \\ \frac{1}{4}=\frac{3 \times 10^{4}}{r} \\ r=12 \times 10^{4} \end{array}$ orbital speed$ of S_{2}$ seen from planet $=\omega_{2} $r$\begin{array}{l} =\frac{2 \pi}{24} \times12 \times10^{4} \\ =\pi \times10^{4} \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}\\ \mathrm{~V}_{1}=\omega_{1} \mathrm{r}_{1}=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \times3 \times10^{4} \\ \Rightarrow 2 \pi \times10^{4} \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1} \end{array}$
$\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}+\frac{2 \pi}{24}\right) \mathrm{t}=\pi\frac{9 \mathrm{t}}{24}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{t}=\frac{12}{9} \mathrm{hr}$ Angle rotate by both satellite $\begin{array}{l} \theta_{1}=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \times \frac{12}{9} \Rightarrow \frac{8 \pi}{9}$ \\ \theta_{2}=$\frac{2 \pi}{24} \times \frac{12}{9}$ \Rightarrow $\frac{\pi}{9} \end{array}$ velocity of $S_{2}$ seen from $S_{1}=V_{1}+V_{2}$ =3 $\pi \times$10^{4} $\mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}$

questions.q: A spiral galaxy can be approximated as an infinitesimally thin disc of a uniform surface mass density (mass per unit area) located at $z = 0,$ Two stars $A$ and $B$ start from rest from heights $2{z}_{0}$ and ${z}_{0}$ (${z}_{0} < <$ radial extent of the disc), respectively and fall towards the disc, cross over to the other side and execute periodic oscillations. The ratio of time periods of $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
Spiral galaxies consists of flat rotating disc containing stars, gas and dust.

Now, we thought of spiral galaxy in form of a disc.

Gravitational intensity at distance $r$$r$ over axis is

${I}_{g} = \dfrac{2GM}{{a}^{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{r}{{\left({r}^{2} + {a}^{2}\right)}^{1 / 2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{2GM}{{a}^{2}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right)}^{1 / 2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{2GM}{{a}^{2}}\left(1 - {\left(1 + \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right)}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}\right)$

Using binomial approximation, we have
${I}_{g} \approx \dfrac{2GM}{{a}^{2}}\left(1 - 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{a}^{2}}{{r}^{2}}\right) \approx \dfrac{2GM}{{r}^{2}}$

So, forces on planet $A$ and $B$ are
${F}_{A} = \dfrac{2GM{m}_{A}}{4{z}_{0}^{2}}, {F}_{B} = 2GM{m}_{B}{z}_{0}^{2}$

Accelerations of $A$ and $B$ respectively, are
${a}_{A} = \dfrac{GM}{2{z}_{0}^{2}}$ and ${a}_{B} = 2GM{z}_{0}^{2}$

If ${T}_{A}$ and ${T}_{B}$ are time periods of oscillations of $A$ and $B$, then

$\dfrac{{T}_{A}}{{T}_{B}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{a}_{B}}{{a}_{A}}}$ [we use $T ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a}}$ as in case of a linear oscillator]

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{1}} ⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{A}}{{T}_{B}} = 2$
